newsitem.title: RUSSIA: LUKoil expects to issue level-3 ADRs Q1 1998.
newsitem.headline: LUKoil expects to issue level-3 ADRs Q1 1998.

text.p: Russia's biggest oil company LUKoil said on Friday it expects to issue level-three American Depositary Receipts in the first quarter of 1998.
LUKoil spokesman Pyotr Neyev said the ADRs could be issued later this year if an audit of three years of LUKoil figures is completed by August by international accountants KPMG.
"It is dependent on KPMG. If they are successful in preparing the balance sheets for three years by August, say, we think we will manange to issue level-three ADRs by the end of 1997," Neyev said.
"But I wouldn't be that optimistic really. I would rather say the first quarter of 1998."
LUKoil originally announced plans in February this year to sell a 15 percent stake of government owned stock to non-strategic investors in the form of level-three ADRs.
LUKoil Vice-President Leonid Fedun said then that the stake would probably be sold in a commercial tender with investment conditions.
He said a consortium or consortia of Russian and foreign banks was likely to win the tender and redistribute the shares in ADR form.
ADRs allow shares to be traded on foreign markets and ease custody and settlement problems common in developing and emerging markets.
The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission must conduct a thorough review of a company's accounts before granting permission for an ADR issue.
Unlike level-one ADRs, which are issued on existing company stock, level-three ADRs raise new capital, and are subject to even more stringent SEC rules.

LUKoil received permission from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission in February to issue level-one ADRs on preferred shares and ADRs on the company's ordinary shares are listed in Berlin, Frankfurt and on the NASDAQ bulletin board.
